title: 10 Features YouTube Users Keep Asking For (Riftn Already Has Them)
html:
YouTube users want simple things. They want to see dislikes. They want their subscriptions in order. They want fewer ads, real messages and a fair cut for creators. Every year they ask, and every year YouTube ships something else.

In 2026 YouTube went further. It cut the dislike button from Shorts, tested hiding it on long videos, removed viewer clips, moved the Subscriptions tab and stretched unskippable ads to 30 seconds on TVs.

We tracked the requests that keep coming back on Reddit, on YouTube's own forums and in the tech press, then checked each one against the Riftn code. Every feature below ships today.

The 10 requests at a glance

  1. Bring back dislikes.
  2. Give me my subscriptions in time order.
  3. Cut the ads.
  4. Let viewers clip again.
  5. Bring back private messages.
  6. Pay creators from day one.
  7. Take a smaller cut.
  8. Stop the bot bans.
  9. Let me take my audience with me.
  10. Build what we actually ask for.

1. Bring back dislikes

What users ask for: a visible dislike count, so they can spot a fake tutorial or a scam before they waste ten minutes on it.

What YouTube did: it hid public dislike counts in November 2021. In July 2026 it retired the dislike button on Shorts and told users to tap "Not interested" instead. In October 2026 it began testing long videos with the dislike button tucked into the three-dot menu. Marques Brownlee said in March 2026 that he would bring the button back if he ran YouTube.

What Riftn does: every post carries a thumbs-down, Shorts included. When dislikes outnumber likes, the post wears a thumbs-down with the dislike count for everyone to see. Posts the crowd rejects drop out of public discovery, so votes do real work.

2. Give me my subscriptions in time order

What users ask for: the people they subscribed to, newest first, without an algorithm in the way.

What YouTube did: in early 2026 some users lost the list view on the Subscriptions feed and saw Shorts mixed into every other row. In November 2026 YouTube moved the Subscriptions tab off the bottom bar and dropped its Today, Unwatched and Live filters.

What Riftn does: the home feed opens on Latest, in time order. Following shows only the people you follow, newest first. You can file creators into follow groups and read one group at a time, the subscription folders YouTube users have wanted for a decade. Hide watched clears out what you have already seen.

3. Cut the ads

What users ask for: fewer interruptions, and no ad wall in the middle of a video.

What YouTube did: it raised unskippable ads on TVs from 15 to 30 seconds in 2026. In July, desktop users reported three ads back to back and unskippable breaks every few minutes.

What Riftn does: ads never interrupt a video. A sponsored card sits in the feed after every eight posts, and one switch in Settings stretches that to every sixteen. Kids mode shows no ads at all. Riftn Premium removes them completely.

4. Let viewers clip again

What users ask for: a clip button, to share the best 30 seconds of a long stream.

What YouTube did: in April 2026 it removed viewer clipping. Only creators can now cut clips, inside YouTube Studio.

What Riftn does: every live stream and replay has a Clip button. Live, it grabs the last minute. On a replay, it opens the editor at your spot. The clip posts as a Short on its own page, crediting both the streamer and the person who clipped it.

5. Bring back private messages

What users ask for: a way to message a creator or a friend without leaving the app.

What YouTube did: it shut down in-app messages in 2019. Late in 2025 it began testing messages again for some adults in Ireland and Poland, and warned that its systems may scan them.

What Riftn does: Messages are end-to-end encrypted, so only you and the person you talk to can read them. Creators can also charge for DMs, so fans who want a reply can pay for one.

6. Pay creators from day one

What users ask for: a way to earn before you hit an arbitrary number.

What YouTube did: the Partner Program asks for 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 watch hours before ads pay a cent. In August 2026 YouTube announced a higher bar from February 2027: 8,000 watch hours, or 20 million Shorts views in 90 days.

What Riftn does: no threshold. Fans can tip you on your first post, and the tip lands in your own wallet on chain the moment they send it. Viewers earn rewards for watching too.

7. Take a smaller cut

What users ask for: more of the money fans spend.

What YouTube did: YouTube keeps 45% of long-form ad revenue and 30% of Super Chat and channel memberships.

What Riftn does: the standard platform fee is 10%. Each badge tier cuts it further, down to 1% for the top tier, so creators keep up to 99%. And Riftn shares 100% of platform profit with $RIFT stakers, so the people who use the network also own a share of what it earns.

8. Stop the bot bans

What users ask for: a human who reads the appeal before a channel disappears.

What YouTube did: in late 2025, creators lost whole channels to automated enforcement. Some appeals came back rejected within minutes. Several channels returned only after the story went viral, and YouTube's CEO defended its AI moderation.

What Riftn does: moderation starts with the community. Reports from long-standing members carry more weight, and posts the crowd rejects drop out of public feeds. A small team handles only what the law requires. Mint a post, and Riftn writes its full text to the blockchain, where nobody can edit or erase it.

9. Let me take my audience with me

What users ask for: a way to leave without starting from zero.

What YouTube did: your subscribers belong to YouTube. Lose the channel, and you lose the audience.

What Riftn does: your wallet is your identity, so no company owns your account. Export everything you have built, including follows, bookmarks, follow groups and blocks, as one file, and import it into another account. People on Mastodon and the rest of the fediverse can follow you at @yourname@riftn.com. Moving in? The YouTube migration tool imports your channel's videos in bulk.

10. Build what we actually ask for

What users ask for: a platform that listens.

What YouTube did: it removes features users love and ships ones nobody asked for, on a roadmap you cannot see.

What Riftn does: anyone can post a request on the features page, and the team builds it in public. If a feature suits everyone, it ships as a default. If it suits only you, it lives in your settings. Open the Builder, describe a mini app in plain words, and the Riftn assistant builds and hosts it for you. The web and mobile apps are open source on GitHub.

A small bonus: set 1.5x speed on a slow talker and Riftn remembers it for that creator only. Everyone else plays at normal speed. YouTube viewers install extensions to get that.

Why YouTube says no

YouTube earns most of its money from ads. Every request on this list costs it something. Dislike counts embarrass advertisers. A feed in time order cuts watch time. Fewer ads mean less revenue. A smaller cut means smaller margins. Portable audiences make leaving easy.

Riftn removes that conflict. Riftn is a social media protocol its users own. Stakers share 100% of platform profit, and badge holders vote on how it runs. When the owners and the users are the same people, the wishlist gets built.

How to switch from YouTube

  1. Join free on riftn.com, Android or iPhone. Sign in with Google, Apple, email or a wallet.
  2. Bring your videos with the YouTube migration tool, or upload them yourself.
  3. Tell your audience where to find you. Your handle works across the fediverse too.
  4. Ask for what is still missing on the features page.

Want the full move plan? Read the creator's guide to leaving YouTube, then see how Riftn ranks against Bluesky, Mastodon and the rest in the top 10 alternative social media apps of 2026.

FAQ

Does Riftn show dislike counts?

Yes. Every post, including Shorts, has a thumbs-down. When dislikes outnumber likes, the post shows the dislike count to everyone.

Can I sort my feed by newest first on Riftn?

Yes. The home feed opens on Latest, in time order, and the Following feed shows only the people you follow, newest first.

Does Riftn have ads?

Yes, but never inside a video. A sponsored card appears after every eight posts, or every sixteen if you ask for fewer. Kids mode has none, and Premium removes them.

How many subscribers do I need to earn on Riftn?

None. Fans can tip you from your first post, and tips land in your own wallet.

Can I move my YouTube channel to Riftn?

Yes. The YouTube migration tool at riftn.com/migrate-youtube imports your videos in bulk.

Sources: Android Authority (November 2026, April 2026, July 2026), Dexerto (July 2026), Ubergizmo (October 2026), UNILAD Tech (March 2026, November 2025), PiunikaWeb (February 2026), Search Engine Journal and PPC Land (December 2025), and YouTube's August 2026 Partner Program announcement.
